rationale: C16 is an unmistakable drafting template for the child. It uses nearly identical language and the same operative sequence: close specified federal offices on December 24 and December 31; excuse metropolitan and field-service employees subject to the same two exceptions; and treat the periods as holidays for compensation and leave. The child principally changes the 1953 dates and makes December 24 a full day rather than a half day. C15 and C04 contain earlier versions of the same closure-and-excusal formula, but neither matches the child's complete two-date and holiday-treatment structure as closely as C16.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the several executive departments, independent establishments, and other governmental agencies in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia, including the General Accounting Office, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations, shall be closed all day on Friday, December 24, 1954 ... and one-half day on Friday, December 31, 1954
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the several executive departments, independent establishments, and other governmental agencies in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia, including the General Accounting Office, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations, shall be closed one-half day on Thursday, December 24, 1953 ... and one-half day on Thursday, December 31, 1953
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces C16's distinctive enumeration of offices, two-date holiday schedule, and sentence structure, altering only the year, weekdays, and duration of the December 24 closure.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: except those who may for special public reasons be excluded from the provisions of this order by the heads of their respective departments, establishments, or agencies, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent with the provisions of existing law
shared_material.explanation: This lengthy two-part exception is copied verbatim within the same operative position.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such day and one-half day shall each be considered a holiday within the meaning of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 9, 1952, and of all statutes so far as they relate to the compensation and leave of employees of the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: each such one-half day shall be considered a holiday within the meaning of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 9, 1952, and of all statutes so far as they relate to the compensation and leave of employees of the United States
shared_material.explanation: The child retains C16's specific legal machinery for treating the excused periods as holidays, adapting the wording to one full day and one half day.
